subject: Temporary fair-share waiver and latency SLA addendum for Helix AI launch
messages:
From: Simon Bradley <simon.bradley@helixai.com>
To: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixai.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary fair-share waiver + latency uplift for 72h launch window

Hi Priya —

We're ramping the public launch of our new realtime assistant next week and expect a concentrated traffic spike that will exceed our current committed throughput. High-level ask: can Redwood provide a temporary fair-share waiver and tightened p95 latency target for one route (/generate) for a 72-hour window during our launch?

Details:
- Window: 2027-06-24 01:00 UTC -> 2027-06-27 01:00 UTC (72 hrs)
- Expected peak QPS: ~2.5x our baseline (sustained bursts up to 3x for short periods)
- Endpoint: /v1/generation (latency-sensitive; user-facing)
- Desired latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms (current default p95 target is 150ms)
- Reason: marketing push + nighttime release in APAC; loss in latency directly impacts conversion

Can you outline operational and commercial terms (temporary uplift, monitoring, rollback triggers, and any one-time fee or short-term commitment)? I've attached a traffic projection.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

Simon
VP Product, Helix AI
[sent from phone]

[Attachment: helix_load_projection.csv]

From: priya_natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary fair-share waiver + latency uplift for 72h launch window

Thanks Simon — and congrats on the launch. Quick acknowledgement and a couple of clarifying asks so we scope the exception correctly: 

- Can you confirm the exact UTC start/end times (you listed a window — want to ensure DST/zone alignment)?
- What's your expected sustained QPS vs short spike QPS? (you mentioned 2.5x / 3x but a per-minute breakdown helps our autoscaling plan)
- Which models/variants and which route(s) should be included in the waiver (you called out /v1/generation — any secondary endpoints?)
- Is any user data in the requests classified as regulated/PII (affects private deployment controls)?

I'll loop in Ben from Sales to capture the commercial terms and Karthik from Platform to validate the operational feasibility. If you can send a contact for billing/PO that speeds procurement.

I'll get you an initial feasibility note + pricing sketch within 24 business hours.

— Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Request: temporary fair-share waiver + latency uplift for 72h launch window

Hi Simon — looping in procurement as requested. We can support a temporary waiver, but there are two common commercial approaches I want to float: 

1) Short-term reserved uplift: commit to a 2-week reserved uplift on Dedicated capacity (reduced unit price relative to on-demand) + one-time provisioning fee.
2) Temporary burst allowance: no long-term commit, a one-time surge fee based on projected token consumption and the increased SLA costs.

For quoting I need: projected token volume for the window (rough), and whether you're open to a 2-week minimum reserved uplift vs pure surge. Either way we'll include a short SLA addendum that limits the waiver to the specified routes and hours.

I've attached a draft SLA addendum with redlines on scope/rollback triggers for your legal and ops review.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Simon / team — operational feasibility note from infra: 

Summary: we can grant a temporary fair-share waiver scoped to Helix AI's account and to the /v1/generation route for the requested 72-hour window with these caveats and controls.

Operational controls we require:
- Pre-warm KV cache for prediction prefixes 12 hours before the window starts.
- Enable temporary routing to prioritised queue with autoscaling enabled and a defined burst cap of 3x baseline.
- Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 250ms for 15 minutes OR error rate > 2% for 10 minutes -> auto rollback to standard fair-share policies.
- Canary: start with a 4-hour soft uplift (partial traffic sampling) before opening full capacity.
- Monitoring: Helix must provide a token-volume projection and a Slack pager contact for the launch window.

Fallbacks: if underlying GPU capacity becomes constrained, we will automatically degrade to a smaller model variant that preserves availability at a slightly higher latency. Customer will be notified via the designated on-call channel.

We will prepare the feature flag and rollout playbook; need confirmation by EOD Thu 2027-06-17 to meet provisioning lead times.

— Karthik
Director, Platform Reliability
